notes:
**A page that arrives as an empty JavaScript shell can no longer testify that your site is missing things.**

On sites that render their content in the browser, Docket was reading the shell's silence as the site's: no H1, no share card, a canonical pointing somewhere else, duplicate titles, missing analytics, too few internal links. Every one of those was a claim about content Docket had never seen.

Measured on a live airline site that serves one byte-identical 37 KB shell for 23 URLs across 18 sections: **eight false findings removed, and both true ones kept.** Those pages are still reported as JavaScript-dependent and still counted as invisible to AI crawlers — that finding is the point of the crawl, and it survives.

Two smaller things in the same release: the analytics finding now says which pages its number is drawn from when some could not be read, and the read-out is unchanged on every site that has no such pages.
